readiness.summary: This app needs changes before Deployz can deploy it.

findings.title: Runs as several services
findings.whyItMatters: Deployz provisions one container per application with managed database, cache, and storage. Extra infrastructure the app expects would not exist at runtime.
findings.suggestedOutcome: Build an image that runs only the web process, and declare each other process as a worker.
findings.technicalEvidence: Unsupported container setup: Dockerfile runs s6-overlay with 19 long-running services (init-complete, init-custom-init, init-env-file, init-folders) in one container. Deployz runs one web process and declared workers as separate services.
findings.plainEnglishExplanation: This app's image starts several long-running processes (web, API, worker) under a supervisor, but Deployz runs one process per container.

findings.title: Files stored on local disk
findings.whyItMatters: Anything written to local disk disappears when the app restarts or updates, so uploads and generated files would be lost.
findings.suggestedOutcome: Store uploaded and persistent files in object storage instead of the local disk.
findings.technicalEvidence: Durable local filesystem state declared: VOLUME /usr/src/paperless/data (Dockerfile)
findings.plainEnglishExplanation: This app writes files to its own disk, but Deployz runs apps on disks that are wiped on every deploy.

findings.title: Database migrations run when the application starts
findings.whyItMatters: Deployz does not run a migration step of its own for this app — the running application updates its own database schema on boot.
findings.suggestedOutcome: No action needed — migrations run on application startup and Deployz monitors the app until it reports healthy.
findings.technicalEvidence: Migrations run at startup: python manage.py migrate (docker/rootfs/etc/s6-overlay/s6-rc.d/init-migrations/run).
findings.plainEnglishExplanation: This app applies its database migrations when the application itself starts, not as a separate deploy step.

findings.title: Background job runner
findings.whyItMatters: Deployz runs one web process per application. Background jobs only run when the web process itself processes them.
findings.suggestedOutcome: Process background jobs inside the web process, or remove the job-runner code if it is not used.
findings.plainEnglishExplanation: This app appears to run background jobs, but no command exists that starts a job runner as a separate process.
